```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("../setup.R")
docs_setup()
```

The z scale maps heights from data units into panel positions and controls their transformations, categories, limits and facets. Set `coord_3d(z_scales = "free")` for separate z ranges across facets. ggplot2 facets have no z scale. Installation is covered in [Get started](ggplot3d.html). For repeated camera views, see [Choosing camera views](camera.html); [Combining 2D and 3D graphics](combining-2d-3d.html#small-multiples-in-depth) stacks two-dimensional panels in depth.

```{r packages, message = FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggplot3d)
```

## Transforming heights

A position scale trains its range from layer data and supplies breaks and labels. The z position family includes z, zmin, zmax, zend and zintercept. A logarithmic transformation therefore also applies to the endpoints of segments.

```{r log, fig.alt="Three vertical segments with endpoints on a logarithmic height scale."}
d <- data.frame(x = 1:3, y = c(1, 2, 1), z = c(1, 10, 100),
                top = c(10, 100, 1000))
ggplot(d, aes(x, y, z = z, xend = x, yend = y, zend = top)) +
  geom_segment_3d(linewidth = 0.8, colour = "#2E6F9E") +
  scale_z_log10(breaks = c(1, 10, 100, 1000)) + coord_3d()
```

Use positive values with a logarithmic scale. `scale_z_sqrt()` compresses large values less strongly, and `scale_z_reverse()` turns the axis upside down, which suits depths below a surface.

```{r reverse, fig.alt="Three points at depths of one, ten and one hundred metres, with the deepest point at the bottom of a reversed axis."}
ggplot(d, aes(x, y, z = z)) + geom_point_3d(size = 3, colour = "#2E6F9E") +
  scale_z_reverse(name = "depth (m)") + coord_3d()
```

Other continuous transformations go through the `transform` argument of `scale_z_continuous()`.

## Categories and dates

A discrete scale places categories at separate z positions in factor-level order. Dates and date-times use their corresponding scale constructors and accept date breaks and labels.

```{r categories, fig.alt="Three points at the low, middle and high category levels."}
categories <- data.frame(x = 1:3, y = c(1, 2, 1),
  stage = factor(c("low", "middle", "high"), levels = c("low", "middle", "high")))
ggplot(categories, aes(x, y, z = stage)) + geom_point_3d(size = 3) +
  scale_z_discrete(name = "Stage") + coord_3d()
```

```{r dates, fig.alt="Three points at dates spaced one day apart."}
dated <- data.frame(x = 1:3, y = c(1, 2, 1),
                    day = as.Date("2026-01-01") + 0:2)
ggplot(dated, aes(x, y, z = day)) + geom_point_3d(size = 3) +
  scale_z_date(date_labels = "%d %b") + coord_3d()
```

Durations such as elapsed hours use `scale_z_time()`, which labels the axis as hours, minutes and seconds.

```{r times, fig.alt="Three points at one, two and three hours of elapsed time."}
dated$elapsed <- as.difftime(1:3, units = "hours")
ggplot(dated, aes(x, y, z = elapsed)) + geom_point_3d(size = 3) +
  scale_z_time() + coord_3d()
```

## Scale limits and coordinate limits

Scale limits participate in data handling before statistical computations. Coordinate limits set the displayed box. Set coordinate limits to inspect part of a surface while retaining the data used to construct it.

```{r limits, fig.alt="Points viewed within a z range from zero to one hundred."}
ggplot(d, aes(x, y, z = z)) + geom_point_3d(size = 3) +
  coord_3d(zlim = c(0, 100))
```

The shorthand `zlim()` supplies scale limits in original data units. Coordinate limits also use original units. [Building surfaces and solids](surfaces-solids.html) explains the transformed units used by statistical surfaces.

## Facets

Facets divide the data into separate panels. By default panels share a z range. Set `coord_3d(z_scales = "free")` to train a separate z range per panel. ggplot2 facets have no z scale; their `scales` argument controls x and y.

```{r facets, fig.alt="Two side-by-side panels with separate z ranges, 1 to 3 for site a and 20 to 60 for site b."}
faceted <- data.frame(x = rep(1:3, 2), y = rep(c(1, 2, 1), 2),
  z = c(1, 2, 3, 20, 40, 60), site = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 3))
ggplot(faceted, aes(x, y, z = z)) + geom_point_3d(size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~site, labeller = label_both) +
  coord_3d(z_scales = "free")
```

Free x and y ranges remain controlled by ggplot2's facet arguments. Use fixed z ranges when equal heights should occupy equal positions across panels.

## Guides and themes

A guide draws breaks, tick labels and an axis title. The z guide uses an exterior edge of the projected box. Theme elements for z inherit the corresponding general axis settings.

```{r guide, fig.alt="Three points with a Height axis title and a blue z axis."}
ggplot(d, aes(x, y, z = z)) + geom_point_3d(size = 3) +
  scale_z_continuous(name = "Height", guide = guide_axis_3d(n.dodge = 1)) +
  coord_3d() + theme(axis.title.z = element_text(colour = "#2E6F9E"))
```

[Styling axes, legends and panes](guides-themes.html) shows edge-following
labels, a colourbar aligned with height and theme elements for individual panes.
